panels.title: Overview — is the relay healthy right now?
Request rate
panels.description: Total HTTP requests served per second across all endpoints.

panels.title: Error ratio (5xx)
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx status.

panels.title: Client rejects (4xx)
panels.description: Share of requests rejected with a 4xx status. High values usually mean bad builder submissions, not a relay fault.

panels.title: Timeout rate
panels.description: Requests that were dropped before the handler recorded a status. This counts client cancellations and server-side timeouts.

panels.title: p99 API latency
panels.description: 99th percentile end-to-end request latency over all endpoints.

panels.title: Pending requests
panels.description: Requests in flight. A rising floor means the relay does not drain its inbound queue.

panels.title: Top-bid stream clients
panels.description: Open top-bid websocket/stream connections.

panels.title: Sim success ratio
panels.description: Share of block simulations that returned success.

panels.title: Throughput by endpoint
panels.description: Requests per second per endpoint. Use this to see which API carries the load.

panels.title: p99 latency by endpoint
panels.description: 99th percentile latency per endpoint. The slowest endpoint here is the first bottleneck candidate.

panels.title: Error ratio by endpoint
panels.description: Per-endpoint 5xx ratio.

targets.expr: sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_request_status_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", endpoint=~"$endpoint", http_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_request_status_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", endpoint=~"$endpoint"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Pending requests by endpoint
panels.description: Concurrency per endpoint. Saturation shows up here before it shows up in latency.

panels.title: Request latency quantiles (all endpoints)
panels.description: Latency spread for the selected endpoints. A wide p50-to-p99 gap means tail problems, not a uniform slowdown.

panels.title: Request latency distribution
panels.description: Full latency histogram over time. Bands that drift upward show a developing bottleneck.

panels.title: Body read latency p99 by step
panels.description: Time to take the request body apart: 'read' is socket read time, 'wait' is time blocked on the client, 'gap' is idle time between polls. A large 'wait' points at the builder's link, not at the relay.

panels.title: Body read latency p99 by endpoint and step
panels.description: Same breakdown split per endpoint.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, endpoint, step) (rate(helix_request_body_latency_secs_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", endpoint=~"$endpoint"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Status codes
panels.description: Response status mix for the selected endpoints.

panels.title: Request size p99
panels.description: 99th percentile request body size. Growing payloads raise read and decode cost.

panels.title: Ingress bytes
panels.description: Inbound request bytes per second per endpoint.

panels.title: Timeouts by endpoint
panels.description: Requests that never recorded a status code, per endpoint.

panels.title: Submission trace p99 by step
panels.description: 99th percentile time spent in each submission stage. The tallest bar is the pipeline bottleneck.

panels.title: Submission trace p50 by step
panels.description: Median time per submission stage. Compare with p99 to tell a constant cost from a tail spike.

panels.title: Submission trace mean by step
panels.description: Mean time per stage.

panels.title: Submission stage throughput
panels.description: How many submissions pass through each stage per second. A stage with a lower rate than the stage before it drops work.

panels.title: Client to server latency
panels.description: Time from the builder's send timestamp to the relay's first packet, per protocol. This is network and builder cost, not relay cost.

panels.title: Submission rate by encoding and compression
panels.description: Submissions per second, split by wire format.

panels.title: Decompression latency p99
panels.description: 99th percentile decompression time per algorithm.

panels.title: Decode latency p99
panels.description: 99th percentile payload decode time per encoding.

panels.title: Compression ratio
panels.description: Decompressed bytes divided by compressed bytes. A fall here means builders send less compressible blocks.

panels.title: Submission bytes on the wire
panels.description: Inbound submission bytes per second, before and after decompression.

panels.title: Decompress size-hint error p99
panels.description: Relative error of the decompressed-size estimate. A large error causes buffer re-allocation during decode.

panels.title: Bid sorter process latency
panels.description: Time the sorter takes for one pass. The sorter is single-threaded, so this time sets the ceiling on bid throughput.

panels.title: Sorter throughput and top-bid updates
panels.description: Sorter passes and resulting top-bid changes per second.

panels.title: Sorter duty cycle
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the sorter spends processing. Near 1.0 means the sorter is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Bid creation and signing latency p99
panels.description: Cost to build and to re-sign the builder bid served by getHeader.

panels.title: Top-bid stream connections
panels.description: Open top-bid stream connections.

panels.title: Hydration cache hits
panels.description: Hydration cache hits per second by order type. A fall here means more full re-hydration work.

panels.title: getPayload trace p99 by step
panels.description: 99th percentile time in each getPayload stage. getPayload is on the proposer's critical path, so any step above a few milliseconds is a risk.

panels.title: getPayload trace p50 by step
panels.description: Median time in each getPayload stage.

panels.title: getPayload total latency
panels.description: End-to-end getPayload latency measured at the HTTP layer.

panels.title: getHeader total latency
panels.description: End-to-end getHeader latency measured at the HTTP layer.

panels.title: getHeader timeouts
panels.description: getHeader gave up waiting for a bid. A rise means the auction did not deliver a bid in time.

panels.title: getPayload failures
panels.description: Failures to publish the block to the beacon clients, and V1 responses held back by the safety buffer.

panels.title: Merge trace p99 by step
panels.description: 99th percentile time in each block-merge stage.

panels.title: Merge trace p50 and throughput
panels.description: Median merge-stage time and merge rate.

panels.title: Sim rate
panels.description: Simulation requests per second.

panels.title: Sim p99 latency
panels.description: 99th percentile simulation latency across all simulators.

panels.title: Sims dropped
panels.description: Simulation requests the manager threw away. Any value above zero means the simulators cannot keep up.

panels.title: Stale sim requests
panels.description: Simulation requests that went stale before a simulator took them.

panels.title: Builders demoted
panels.description: Builder demotions per second.

panels.title: Unhealthy simulators
panels.description: Simulators that are not in the OK state.

panels.title: Simulation latency per simulator
panels.description: Simulation latency per simulator. One slow simulator holds back the whole optimistic pipeline.

panels.title: Simulation rate and outcome
panels.description: Simulation requests per second by mode, and results by outcome.

panels.title: Simulator health
panels.description: 0 = ok, 1 = probe, 2 = breaker open, 3 = unsynced.

panels.title: Simulator sync state
panels.description: 1 = synced, 0 = not synced.

panels.title: Simulator concurrency limit
panels.description: Adaptive in-flight limit per simulator. A falling limit means the relay is backing off from a slow simulator.

panels.title: Simulator slot latency (mean, last slot)
panels.description: Mean simulation latency per simulator over the last slot.

panels.title: Sim manager queue state
panels.description: Simulation manager in-flight and pending limits.

panels.title: Sim manager events
panels.description: Simulation manager events per second: requests sent at once, dropped, and stale.

panels.title: Demotions and disabled adjustments
panels.description: Builder demotions and adjustment shut-offs.

panels.title: Beacon node sync state
panels.description: 1 = synced, 0 = not synced.

panels.title: Worker utilization (mean)
panels.description: Fraction of loop time each worker spends on real work. Above roughly 0.8 the worker is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Worker utilization p95
panels.description: 95th percentile worker utilization.

panels.title: Worker queue length p99
panels.description: 99th percentile queue depth per worker queue. A queue that does not return to zero is a backlog.

panels.title: Worker queue length mean
panels.description: Mean queue depth per worker queue.

panels.title: Worker task latency p99
panels.description: 99th percentile time per task type per worker.

panels.title: Worker task rate
panels.description: Tasks processed per second per worker.

panels.title: State transition latency p99 (top 10)
panels.description: Slowest auctioneer state transitions, as start+event->end.

panels.title: State transition rate (top 10)
panels.description: Most frequent auctioneer state transitions.

panels.title: State machine busy time
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time each transition consumes. This shows where the auctioneer loop spends its budget.

panels.title: Bid adjustment latency p99
panels.description: Cost of the bid adjustment path, split into calculation and application.

panels.title: Alive tasks
panels.description: Live tokio tasks.

panels.title: Global queue depth
panels.description: Tasks waiting in the global run queue. A non-zero floor means the runtime is short of worker threads.

panels.title: Scheduling drift
panels.description: Delay between the time a timer was due and the time it ran. This is the clearest sign that the runtime is starved.

panels.title: Spawned tasks
panels.description: Tasks tracked per spawn origin.

panels.title: Scheduling drift
panels.description: Tokio scheduling drift. Spikes line up with latency spikes when the CPU is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Global queue depth and alive tasks
panels.description: Runtime backlog and task count.

panels.title: Tokio worker busy time
panels.description: Busy fraction per tokio worker thread. The exporter writes the busy microseconds of the last one-second window, so the value divided by 1e6 is the duty cycle. Values near 1.0 on every thread mean the process is CPU-bound.

panels.title: Spawned tasks by origin
panels.description: Tracked tasks per spawn origin. Steady growth means a task leak.

panels.title: DB operation rate
panels.description: Database operations per second by call site.

panels.title: DB failure ratio
panels.description: Share of failed database operations per call site.

targets.expr: sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_db_count_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", is_success="false"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_db_count_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: DB latency p99
panels.description: Ten slowest database call sites at the 99th percentile.

panels.title: DB latency p50
panels.description: Ten slowest database call sites at the median.

panels.title: DB time share
panels.description: Wall-clock seconds per second spent in each database call. This finds the call that costs the most in total, not the one that is slowest per call.

panels.title: Cache sizes
panels.description: Entries held in each in-process cache. Unbounded growth is a memory risk.

panels.title: Cache hits
panels.description: Cache hits per second for the data API caches.

panels.title: Gossip message rate
panels.description: Gossip messages per second in each direction.

panels.title: Gossip send failure ratio
panels.description: Share of gossip sends that failed. A rise here means the peer relay or the link is down.

targets.expr: sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_out_gossip_count_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", is_success="false"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (endpoint) (rate(helix_out_gossip_count_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Gossip send latency
panels.description: Time to send a gossip message to the peer relays.

panels.title: Gossip bytes
panels.description: Gossip bytes per second in each direction.

panels.title: Duties age
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful proposer-duties fetch. A rise means the relay works from stale duties.

panels.title: Duties lookahead
panels.description: Slots between the head and the last known duty. A small value means the relay is close to losing proposer coverage.

panels.title: Registration rate
panels.description: Validator registrations checked per second.

panels.title: Invalid registrations
panels.description: Invalid registrations per second.

panels.title: Registration outcomes
panels.description: Validator registration outcomes per second.

panels.title: registerValidator latency
panels.description: End-to-end registerValidator latency.

panels.title: Proposer duties fetch
panels.description: Proposer-duties fetches per second by outcome.

panels.title: Duties freshness
panels.description: Age of the last duties fetch and how far ahead the relay can see.

panels.title: Deployed build
panels.description: Version, commit, branch, build time, and region reported by each relay instance.
